To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ShcΔC, a mutant of the collagen-homology (collagen-homology) domain 1 deletion of Shc, suppresses cellular transformation mediated by neu in NIH3T3 fibroblasts.
a Shc collagen-homology-domain 1-deletion mutant suppresses cellular transformation mediated by neu by a mitogen-activated-protein kinase (MAPK)-independent pathway.
a mutant Shc protein lacking collagen-homology 1 domain suppresses cellular transformation mediated by p185* through a MAPK pathway-independent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel function of Shc, which may be involved in the oncogenesis mediated by activated neu through an unidentified signal pathway.
elucidating the role of Shcs in cellular transformation induced by activated oncogenes.
the role of ShC in the oncogenesis induced by point-mutation activation of the neu oncogene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Shc is involved in the transformation of cells by activated neu through multiple pathways.
Shc plays a dual role in cellular transformation, and that it is a key regulator of multiple signal pathways.
the Grb2/Sos binding site of Shc is not required for Shc-mediated suppression of p185*-mediating transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Shc is involved in both the MAPK and PI3K pathways, and Shc is a critical mediator for cellular transformation.
the collagen-homology 1 domain is essential for Shc to mediate cellular transformation induced by neu.
ShcΔCh1 can suppress the oncogenesis by p185*, but it is not due to the inhibition of the Shc-p185*-Grb2-SOS complex formation, and it is also not due to the disruption of the MAPK pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Shc is not only a positive mediator of cellular transformation, but also a negative regulator of cellular transformation.
the Shc protein is involved in other signaling pathways in addition to the well-known mitogen-activated pathway (MAPK).
the ShcΔCH-1 mutant suppresses transformation mediated through a MAPK independent pathway.
